summary: 新西兰中学考试中男女生的通过率存在差距，阅读写作、选考情况和发展时点都可能参与其中。全国平均数掩盖了社会背景和教学质量的差异，单性别学校的表现也引出了不同解释。

paragraphs.brief: 女生考试优势与历史背景
sentences: The issue is the difference in pass rates between the sexes: at each level of the examination and across all school types, the difference is about 10 percentage points.
问题在于男女生的及格率有差距：无论哪个考试级别、哪类学校，两者都相差约十个百分点。
Girls are doing better in every subject, and those in girls-only schools are taking top honours.
女生在每门学科的表现都更好，女子学校的学生更是名列前茅。
The results are not a surprise: high school girls have been outperforming boys academically for more than a decade.
这一结果并不意外，高中女生的学业成绩领先男生已有十多年。
It is an international phenomenon, and within Australia was the subject of much debate and controversy.
这是一种国际现象，在澳大利亚也引发了许多讨论和争议。
Within New Zealand back in the 1980s, there was a concerted campaign, called ‘Girls Can Do Anything’, which was aimed at lifting girls’ participation rates, achievement levels and aspirations.
20世纪80年代，新西兰曾大力开展“女孩什么都能做”的运动，旨在提高女生的参与率、学业成就和志向。
This was so successful that the pendulum has now swung to the other extreme.
这项运动非常成功，如今优势似乎已摆到了另一个极端。
Views differ on how worried people should be.
对于这种差距究竟有多值得担忧，人们看法不一。
After all, for much of history, girls were excluded from any form of education, and this new phenomenon could be seen as a temporary over-correction before the balance is righted.
毕竟，在历史上的很长时期，女孩根本没有机会接受教育；因而也可以把当下的现象看成恢复平衡之前暂时出现的矫枉过正。
paragraphs.gist: 新西兰高中女生在各级考试的及格率约高出男生十个百分点，对于这是否只是历史性失衡得到纠正后的暂时现象，各方看法不同。

paragraphs.brief: 教育部门的应对与质疑
sentences: However the New Zealand State Ministry of Education says it is taking the issue seriously.
不过，新西兰教育部表示，它正在认真对待这一问题。

It is working with a reference group on boys’ education which has been set up, and it has commissioned an Australian academic to report on interventions that have been found to work for boys, drawing particularly on Australia’s experience.
教育部正与新成立的男生教育咨询小组合作，并委托一名澳大利亚学者重点参考澳大利亚经验，整理哪些干预措施已被证实对男生有效。

But some, such as former prison manager Celia Lashlie, the author of a book for parents of teenage boys, believe there is still resistance within the Education Ministry towards doing anything about the problem.
但也有人认为，教育部内仍有阻止采取行动的阻力，其中包括前监狱管理者西莉亚·拉什利，她曾为青春期男孩的父母写过一本书。
paragraphs.gist: 新西兰教育部组建男生教育咨询小组并委托学者评估澳洲有效做法，但也有人认为部内仍不愿采取行动。

paragraphs.brief: 分项成绩显示读写差距
sentences: Education Ministry learning policy manager Steve Benson says that the ‘National Certificate in Educational Achievement’, or NCEA, as New Zealand’s high school exams are called, is useful to employers and to universities because it provides a fine-grained picture of pupils’ performance in every aspect of a subject, rather than just a pass or fail in an overall area.
教育部学习政策负责人史蒂夫·本森说，新西兰高中考试NCEA（全国教育成就证书）能细致反映学生在一门学科各方面的表现，而不仅仅给出总体及格或不及格，因此对雇主和大学都很有用。
‘In most parts of the curriculum, for example in maths, there isn’t really a gender gap.
“大多数课程内容，例如数学，其实没有明显的性别差距。
But literacy is a different matter.
不过，读写能力是另一回事。
Even boys who are good at writing tend not to write so much.
即使是擅长写作的男生，往往也写得不多。
There’s actually a quantity issue.’
实际存在的是写作量的差异。”
paragraphs.gist: 教育部门认为，NCEA细分学科表现后显示，多数领域如数学没有明显性别差距，读写方面则连擅长写作的男生也往往写得较少。

paragraphs.brief: 读写能力为何日益重要
sentences: The discrepancy in reading and writing skills between males and females shows up as early as preschool, and the difference is clear by the time these children enter high school.
男女在读写能力方面的差距早在学龄前就显现出来，在这些儿童进入高中时，差距就很明显。
Not being good at literacy was not such a problem in the old days when many students left school for manual jobs after Year 11.
过去不少学生十一年级后就离校从事体力劳动，读写能力较弱还不算太大的问题。
But nowadays many more stay on to higher education, and almost all jobs require literacy skills.
但如今还有更多的人继续接受高等教育，几乎所有工作都需要识字技能。

Roger Moses, the headmaster of Wellington College, says that the written content of NCEA papers is more demanding than the previous system of secondary school qualifications in New Zealand, even in subjects such as statistics and accounting.
惠灵顿学院校长罗杰·摩西说，NCEA考卷对书面作答的要求比过去的中学资格考试更高，即便在统计和会计等科目也是如此。
paragraphs.gist: 读写差距可追溯到学龄前，随着升学和就业越来越依赖读写能力、连统计与会计也要求更多书面作答，其影响更加突出。

paragraphs.brief: 群体内部差异超出性别差异
sentences: New Zealand 15-year-olds do very well in international reading tests, but beneath this average lies a wide variance, with New Zealand European girls most represented at the top and New Zealand Pacific Island boys at the bottom.
新西兰15岁学生在国际阅读测验中的总体表现很好，但平均值掩盖了很大的差异：高分群体中以欧裔女生最为突出，而太平洋岛裔男生较多处于低分端。
Yet some European girls drop out, and some Pacific Island boys excel.
不过，也有欧裔女生退学，有太平洋岛裔男生成绩优异。
In other words, the range in performance within each gender group is much greater than the gender differences.
换句话说，各性别群体内部的成绩差异，远大于男女两组之间的差距。
Ethnic differences, and differences in socio-economic status, may be more significant than the simple boy/girl explanation.
比起简单用男女性别作解释，族裔与社会经济地位的差别也许更有解释力。
paragraphs.gist: 新西兰15岁学生的平均阅读成绩虽高，各性别内部的差异却大于两性平均差距，族裔与社会经济条件可能更能解释表现。

paragraphs.brief: 分班成效背后的教师因素
sentences: This makes the Education Ministry nervous about pushing solutions that emphasise stereotyped gender differences, rather than looking at underachievement as a whole.
正因如此，教育部不愿推动只强调性别刻板印象的方案，而希望从整体考察学生成绩不佳的问题。
Rob Burroughs, principal of Linwood High School in Christchurch, agrees.
基督城林伍德高中校长罗布·伯勒斯也赞同这一点。
For three years his school ran separate boys’ classes to try to address the disparity in performance, before abandoning them.
学校曾连续三年开设男生单独班，试图缩小成绩差距，后来放弃了这种做法。
The research showed that the boys did better in their own class than in the co-educational environment.
研究显示，男生单独成班时的成绩优于男女合班。
But when he looked at which teachers they had, and how well those teachers’ other classes did, it became clear that the difference was, instead, to do with the quality of instruction.
但他把任课教师及这些教师所教其他班级的成绩放在一起比较后，发现差别其实来自教学质量。
paragraphs.gist: 一所学校试办男生班后最初看似有效，但对照同一教师带的其他班级才发现，成绩差异更可能来自教学质量。

paragraphs.brief: 男生的成熟与竞争意识
sentences: At Onslow College, Dr Stuart Martin would do away with the NCEA Level 1 exam if he could.
翁斯洛中学的斯图尔特·马丁博士说，如果可以，他会取消NCEA一级考试。
He says that in Year 11, aged 15, boys are simply not mature enough to cope.
他说，十一年级学生约十五岁，男生往往还不够成熟，难以应付这场考试。
‘They tend to think that just passing is enough, and that it’s not necessary to work hard for a Merit or an Excellence grade.
他们往往认为及格便足够，没必要为获得“良好”或“优秀”等级而格外努力。
Often they are busy with other activities and part-time jobs.
他们也常忙于其他活动和兼职工作。
Boys’ competitive instinct tends to come out later in their schooling years, especially if there is money attached or other tangible rewards.
男生的竞争意识往往到在校学习的较后阶段才显现，尤其是奖项涉及金钱或其他实际回报时。
By 17, boys are catching up academically with the girls, and by the end of Year 13, boys are again winning the top prizes.’
到了十七岁，男生的学业成绩逐渐赶上女生；到十三年级结束时，男生又开始赢得最高奖。
paragraphs.gist: 一位校长认为15岁男生常满足于及格，到了17岁竞争心才变强，因而主张取消他们尚不成熟时参加的一级考试。

paragraphs.brief: 男校表现与性别参与机会
sentences: Boys in single-sex schools do better in NCEA across all levels, something economist Brian Easton reported after analysing data from the first year of NCEA’s implementation.
经济学家布赖恩·伊斯顿分析NCEA实施首年的数据后指出，男校学生在各级考试中的表现都较好。
He said the results were valid, even when socio-economic status was taken into account.
他说，即使把家庭社会经济地位考虑在内，这一结果仍然成立。
Dr Paul Baker, head of Waitaki Boys’ High School in Oamaru, agrees.
奥马鲁怀塔基男子中学校长保罗·贝克博士也表示认同。
He thinks that although it is possible for all schools to do more to boost boys’ performance, it is easier in a boys’ school, where activities cannot be ‘captured by girls’.
他认为，每所学校都能设法进一步提高男生成绩，但男校做起来更容易，因为在男校里，活动机会不会被女生占去。
paragraphs.gist: 首年考试数据表明，即使计入社会经济背景，男校学生各级表现仍较好；一位男校校长认为单一性别环境更易让男生参与活动。

items.en: an advantage of New Zealand’s secondary school tests
items.zh: 新西兰中学考试的优点
items.why: 新西兰中学考试能细分同一科目各方面的表现，使雇主和大学得到比简单及格与否更具体的信息。

items.en: a mention of current government initiatives to boost male achievement
items.zh: 提及政府目前为提高男生成绩而采取的举措。
items.why: 直接描述教育部正在进行的举措，且目标是男生表现的改进。

items.en: when gender difference in literacy skills first becomes evident
items.zh: 男女读写能力的差距最早何时开始显现。
items.why: 给出“最早在学前阶段”这一时间点，即题干所问“first becomes evident”。

items.en: findings that relate academic achievement to race
items.zh: 把学业成绩与族群背景联系起来的研究发现。
items.why: 明确把成绩差异与族裔/种族、社会经济地位联系起来，是对题干的直接对应。

items.en: New Zealanders are worried at the outcomes of their high school assessment system, because the ________ of girls are higher than those of boys by 10%.
items.zh: 新西兰人对本国高中评估制度的结果感到担忧，因为女生的________比男生高出 10%。
items.why: 题干中的“higher than…by 10%"” 与原文“差约10个百分点”完全对应。空格所指即“通过率”。

items.en: A gender gap has been apparent for over a ________.
items.zh: 这种性别差距已经明显存在了一个________以上。
items.why: 原文为“十多年 (more than a decade)”。按题目要求写单词 decade。

items.en: This situation is not unique to New Zealand, and has been noticed in ________ also.
items.zh: 这种现象并非新西兰独有，________也出现过类似情况。
items.why: A 段唯一明确点名的新西兰以外国家是 Australia,与题干“also”相呼应。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

items.answer: H · The New Zealand government is reluctant to take action on behalf of boys.
items.solution: 新西兰政府不太愿意为改善男生处境采取行动。

items.answer: E · The difference in achievement between schoolboys and girls is only evident in some subjects.
items.solution: 男生和女生的成绩差异只在某些科目上明显。

items.answer: G · The NCEA exams have higher literacy standards than past exams did.
items.solution: NCEA考试的读写能力要求高于以往考试。

items.answer: C · Good teaching is more important than whether classrooms are single-sex or mixed.
items.solution: 与男女分班或混合编班相比，良好的教学更为重要。

items.answer: F · Older boys are more motivated to study than younger boys.
items.solution: 年龄较大的男孩比年轻男孩更有学习的动力。

items.answer: B · Boys are disadvantaged by girls tending to take over at school.
items.solution: 女生在学校活动中容易占主导，使男生处于不利地位。

points: 明确把成绩差异与族裔/种族、社会经济地位联系起来，是对题干的直接对应。
原文为“十多年 (more than a decade)”。按题目要求写单词 decade。
clauses: Within New Zealand back in the 1980s, there was a concerted campaign, called ‘Girls Can Do Anything’, ….
“which was aimed at lifting girls’ participation rates, achievement levels and aspirations”修饰前面的 campaign。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 campaign，再把修饰信息接回主句。
“that the pendulum has now swung to the other extreme”补足 successful 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 successful 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Results from New Zealand’s new national examinations for secondary schools are giving that country some cause for concern.
新西兰新的中学全国考试的结果使该国感到有些担忧。
vocabulary: 学业表现未达应有水平
